title: Oral Bleeding
portrait_note: Young athletic Black man likeness (hemarthrosis athlete ref), swollen knee hemarthrosis, clutching joint on ED stretcher, light blue hospital gown, MeWorld sculptural CGI clinical still — same face throughout

rationale.PT/PTT / Platelets: PTT prolonged, PT normal, Plt normal — isolated intrinsic pathway defect before you commit to factor replacement.
rationale.Mixing study: PTT corrects — excludes inhibitor; if it fails to correct, think acquired inhibitor not classic hemophilia A.
rationale.Factor VIII assay: Low FVIII activity confirms hemophilia A and guides severity.
rationale.Factor VIII concentrate: Definitive hemostasis for active hemarthrosis — replace what the joint cannot clot without.
rationale.DDAVP (mild hemophilia A): Mild disease may respond to desmopressin releasing stored VIII and vWF — not enough alone for severe bleed.
rationale.Avoid NSAIDs: Antiplatelet effect worsens bleeding — acetaminophen only for pain.
rationale.Avoid IM injections: Intramuscular hematoma risk — IV and PO routes only.
rationale.Physical exam: extremities / joints: Document swollen painful knee, range of motion, and prior hemarthrosis sites — exam drives urgency of factor.
rationale.Supportive care (RICE, joint immobilizat: Rest, ice, compression, elevation, and splint while factor works — protects cartilage from repeat bleed.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a young man with known easy bruising who presents after a trivial twist during pickup soccer — his right knee blew up within hours. He has had prior hemarthrosis in both knees and elbows since childhood. Family history: maternal uncle with "bleeding problems." Labs already show prolonged PTT with normal PT and platelets. Hemophilia A is X-linked recessive Factor VIII deficiency. Mixing study corrects. Active joint bleed needs factor VIII concentrate now; mild disease may also get DDAVP. Never NSAIDs or IM injections.
hpi_narrative:
{{patient_name}} is a young man with known easy bruising who presents after a trivial twist during pickup soccer — his right knee blew up within hours. He has had prior hemarthrosis in both knees and elbows since childhood. Family history: maternal uncle with "bleeding problems."

Mechanism: Factor VIII anchors the intrinsic tenase complex — without it, fibrin cannot stabilize in the joint space, so trivial trauma becomes hemarthrosis. PTT prolongation with normal PT and platelets localizes the defect to Factor VIII, not liver, vitamin K, or platelets.

Workup: coags and mixing study, Factor VIII assay. Treatment: Factor VIII concentrate for active bleed; DDAVP if mild. Avoid NSAIDs and IM injections. Exam the joint, then RICE while factor infuses.
